usageNotes: Use this to create a new network interface definition (bridge, bond, VLAN, static IP, etc.) on a PDM node; the interface is staged in /etc/network/interfaces but does not go live until you apply pending changes via PUT /nodes/{node}/network. Requires System.Modify on the specific interface path, so the token must have that privilege scoped to the target node. Only one interface name (`iface`) may be created per call — for complex topologies (bond + bridge) issue multiple calls in dependency order.

examples.summary: Create a VLAN-aware Linux bridge (vmbr1) with a static IP on node pdm01

params.comments: VM traffic bridge on second NIC

tips: Changes are staged only — run PUT /nodes/{node}/network (apply) or reload the network service to activate; guests may lose connectivity during the apply step.
For VLAN interfaces set type=vlan, vlan-id to the tag, and vlan-raw-device to the parent physical interface.
For 802.3ad bonds set bond_mode=802.3ad and bond_xmit_hash_policy (layer2+3 is the most common choice for balanced hashing).
Interface names must be 15 characters or fewer — an AD-style hostname constraint also enforced by Proxmox.
Setting a gateway here makes this the default route for the node; only one interface should carry a gateway to avoid routing conflicts.
